chunks: And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When a man nurses from the milk of a woman, it becomes forbidden for him to marry all her offspring, even if the offspring are from a man other than the one whose milk she consumed with him; and when he nurses from the milk of a man, it becomes forbidden for him to marry all that man's offspring, even if they are from a woman other than the one who nursed him."

As for the report that Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from Ali ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Bakkar ibn al-Jarrah, from Bistam, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said: "What becomes forbidden through nursing is only the belly (womb) from which the milk was consumed."

The meaning of this is that the prohibition does not extend to those related to the mother through nursing, because such a person is only related to another womb, and what is specific to her womb by birth, that is what becomes forbidden. And when the nursing that causes prohibition occurs, it forbids marriage between the children of the milk-owner and the nursed one.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ اللَّبَنِ: The milk-owner (biological parent of the nursed)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules of marriage prohibition through breastfeeding in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This passage from Tahdhib al-Ahkam highlights the classical juristic debate (khilaf) regarding whether breastfeeding establishes kinship through the mother's womb (biological lineage) or merely creates a spiritual bond with the nursing woman. The reconciliation clarifies that while the milk-consumer becomes mahram to the biological children of the milk-source, the prohibition is rooted in the specific womb that gestated them, distinguishing between biological descent and the act of nursing. This distinction is crucial in Shia fiqh for determining marriage eligibility among extended family members connected via wet-nursing.
